title: Embedded and Edge Systems
description: Resource-constrained design, deterministic scheduling, industrial protocol work, and fail-safe firmware update — the capability to ship software that stays inside a stated memory and latency budget and can be updated without bricking the node.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can complete a guided host-side exercise that stays inside a written memory or latency budget, and can point at the measurement (size report, tick log, or capture) that shows which constraint was binding.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement a scoped edge-style component — ring buffer, cooperative scheduler, or framed protocol — on a host or simulator, produce a measurement that shows the budget was met or missed, and write the failure policy (drop, overwrite, refuse, roll back) in a note a mentor can check.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently design, implement and test a multi-component edge path (producer → buffer → protocol → sink) under stated RAM, stack and deadline limits, and can defend in writing why a general-purpose allocator, blocking retry, or unsigned image is forbidden on that path.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a missed deadline, protocol stall or failed update in a simulated plant, isolate the contributing factor (priority inversion, buffer overflow, unauthenticated image, missing rollback slot), and produce a change that restores the stated invariant.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's edge design, name any unbounded allocation, silent overwrite or unsafe update path in it, and teach the budget-first / fail-safe-update sequence to someone new to constrained systems.
